clinicianRules.rule: dizziness cases should be referred to neurology, and neuro-otology if there is a true vertiginous component or a history of ear or brain surgeries.
definition: • Internal Vertigo: A false sensation of self-motion. The person feels like they are spinning clockwise/counter-clockwise, tilting, or being pulled in a specific direction.
• External Vertigo: A false sensation that the surrounding environment is moving, spinning, or whirling around them.
The direction is often predictable (e.g. "always to the right")
clarification: Vertigo episodes that last between 30 min and 12 hours should count as vertigo for purposes of ruling out meniere's disease, transient vertigo (true room spinning for a few seconds can count as vertigo which can be consistent with migrainous vertigo). A rocking or bobbing sensation is not true vertigo but a dizziness morphology that can be consistent with migrainous symptoms. Also some people describe "the floor falling out from underneath them".

story.intro: A few things about what's been tried already.

migraine.title: Headache pattern
migraine.lede: Migraine doesn't always mean a classic headache. It can show up as pressure across the face and cheeks that feels exactly like a sinus problem.

vestibular.title: Dizziness and ears
vestibular.lede: Dizziness and ear symptoms can come from the same mechanism, even when hearing tests and scans are normal.

neuro.title: Nerve-type symptoms
neuro.lede: Some people get nerve-type symptoms — burning, tingling, or pain that doesn't match what an exam shows.

impact.title: Daily impact
impact.lede: Two quick questions. These tend to carry a lot of weight with clinicians, so it's worth being accurate rather than brave.

discriminators.title: Test results
discriminators.lede: These point away from the pattern this tool looks for, which makes them just as useful. Plenty of people won't know — "Not sure" is genuinely the right answer then.

migraine.title: Patrón de dolor de cabeza
migraine.lede: La migraña no siempre es un dolor de cabeza clásico. Puede aparecer como presión en la cara y los pómulos que se siente igual que un problema de los senos nasales.

vestibular.title: Mareos y oídos
vestibular.lede: Los mareos y los síntomas del oído pueden venir del mismo mecanismo, aunque las pruebas de audición y los estudios salgan normales.

neuro.title: Síntomas de los nervios
neuro.lede: Algunas personas tienen síntomas de los nervios — ardor, hormigueo, o dolor que no corresponde con lo que muestra el examen.

impact.title: Impacto diario
impact.lede: Dos preguntas rápidas. Estas suelen pesar mucho con los médicos, así que vale más ser exacto que valiente.

discriminators.title: Resultados de estudios
discriminators.lede: Estas apuntan en dirección contraria al patrón que busca esta herramienta, lo cual las hace igual de útiles. Mucha gente no lo sabrá — ahí "No estoy seguro" es de verdad la respuesta correcta.

ui.sub: Una herramienta MASQUE · para personas con problemas continuos de senos nasales, oídos o mareos
forYouIf: Lleva meses con síntomas de senos nasales, presión en la cara, oídos o mareos.
Los tratamientos no le han dado alivio duradero, o sus estudios salieron normales y todavía se siente mal.
Ha visto a más de un médico por esto.

emrDetails: **Launch.** The app opens from the chart via a SMART on FHIR EHR launch; the patient banner above is populated from the launch context (here, a sandbox Patient resource).
**Capture.** The clinician or patient completes the short screen; nothing is sent anywhere while answering.
**Write-back.** Results post as FHIR resources — a QuestionnaireResponse, an Observation carrying the MASQUE index and band, and a conditional ServiceRequest for referral — shown in the bundle above.
**Prompt.** A CDS Hooks card surfaces the recommendation in the ordering workflow.
**Privacy.** In deployment, acoustic / free-text features are extracted at the edge and raw identifiable data is not centralized; codes shown here use a placeholder system and are illustrative.

scribe.vmpathiDisclaimer: Screening aid, not a diagnosis. Prompts are authored and mirror the VM-PATHI domains; the validated VM-PATHI is administered under license for confirmation.
about: **Listen.** In this prototype the browser's own speech recognition transcribes the microphone (a deployment runs ambient ASR on-device); rule-based extraction maps what the patient says to MASQUE items as each phrase lands (shown as green capture tags — dashed while a phrase is still being recognised).

**Prompt.** The scribe computes coverage and surfaces only the highest-yield unasked questions for the active pathway — pulling in the VM-PATHI vestibular domains once otologic symptoms appear — so the physician asks what matters without reading a 25-item form aloud.

**Document.** Captured findings, the MASQUE index, and the plan assemble into a draft note and a FHIR bundle (QuestionnaireResponse, Observation, ServiceRequest, DocumentReference) for one-tap sign-off.
**Protect.** No raw audio is retained; only structured findings persist.

Lexicon 0.3.1 → 0.3.2, approved by the clinical lead on 2026-10-04. v_vertigo: heard signal on (heard) and carry-over 2 (carry): when its cue is heard with no duration phrase the item stays unanswered and is shown as heard, and the next two patient replies may supply the duration — same item only; refused when the reply names anything else the lexicon knows, contains the item's own cue, is a question, contains a carryRefuse phrase, or when any duration phrase in it is negated (a negation cue anywhere before it in the reply), its duration phrases disagree, or it is attributed or historical. v_vertigo carry exclusions (carryExclude; clinical-lead decision 2026-10-04, day ranges are same-sentence only): about a day, overnight, for a day or two, for a couple of days, for two days, for three days set the duration only in a sentence where a v_vertigo cue is said, not negated, attributed or historical (a sentence ends at . ! ? or ; followed by whitespace or the end of the text), never from a carried reply; elsewhere in the cue's own utterance, and in a reply, they never supply the duration but still count for the negation and disagreement tests, so an utterance or reply in which one of them disagrees with another duration phrase gives no duration, and one standing alone outside such a sentence is a stated duration that is withheld. In the cue's own utterance a heard entry takes a duration only when the duration phrases found there agree, none of them is negated and no carryRefuse phrase occurs (an onset is not a duration); a phrase inside a longer phrase does not count. A duration that is stated but withheld leaves the item heard, opens only a yield-only slot (it keeps the yieldTo suppression for the next replies and never carries a value), and turns an open slot of that item yield-only with its reply window renewed, so the clinician asks. m_dur yields to v_vertigo (yieldTo) unless an approved anchor phrase is present and not negated, so a dizziness-duration sentence no longer scores the headache-attack duration; the yield holds while the reply window of a heard v_vertigo cue is open, also after its heard card is answered or skipped (an answered or skipped item is never carried); anchors: headache, facial pressure, facial pain, pressure in my face, behind my eyes, migraine lasts, migraines last, head pain. carryRefuse: ago, since, started, began — confirmed by the clinical lead on 2026-10-04 (proposed by the team as a carry-over guard). In a heard entry's own utterance it withholds the duration and no carry-over opens from that utterance; in a carried reply it refuses the carry. It can only prevent a capture, never cause one: withholding a duration no longer arms carry-over, so no later reply can supply a value because of it (an utterance with no duration phrase arms carry-over as before). Text normalization (normalize): before matching, curly apostrophes are read as a straight apostrophe; for duration band phrases only (clinical-lead decision 2026-10-04, digits for durations only), the standalone whole numbers 0–20 and 30, 40 … 90 are read as English words, so typed digits never reach a cue, yes/no, context, multi-item or red-flag phrase or a negation, attribution or history window; every other number stays as digits. Phrases appended: /lexicon/scale/1/cue (v_vertigo cues): world is moving, world moving around, world's moving, world was moving, everything spins, everything spun, room spun, room is moving, everything is moving, like i'm on a boat, like i was on a boat, like i am on a boat, like being on a boat, rocking feeling, rocking sensation, swaying side to side, feel unsteady, unsteady on my feet, losing my balance, lose my balance, balance is off; /lexicon/scale/1/bands/0/ph (v_vertigo, Under 5 min): split second, a second or two, a couple minutes, under five minutes, less than five minutes, two minutes, three minutes, four minutes; /lexicon/scale/1/bands/2/ph (v_vertigo, 5 min – 72 h): half the day, half a day, about a day, all night, for a day or two, for a couple of days, for two days, for three days, overnight; /lexicon/scale/1/bands/1/ph (v_vertigo, Over 72 h): lasts more than three days, lasted more than three days, days at a time; /lexicon/bool/8/ph (v_head): roll over, rolled over, turning over, over in bed, when i turn my head, when i look up, when i lie back, lying back in, tip my head back, high shelf, bending over; /lexicon/bool/6/ph (v_motion): driving through a tunnel, drive through a tunnel, patterned, busy visual, dizzy riding in a car, sick riding in a car; /lexicon/bool/7/ph (v_aural): ears feel full, ears ring, roaring; /lexicon/bool/19/ph (v_migfeat): headache during the dizz, headaches during the dizz; /lexicon/negation/cues: fewer than; /lexicon/thirdParty/cues: my grandmother, my grandma, my aunt, my uncle, my friend. Lexicon 0.3.2 → 0.3.3 (release 0.4.7), from the clinical lead's request and decisions of 2026-10-11, signed off by the clinical lead on 2026-10-12 (sign-off page and chat): every row the team drafted and the lead approved is marked lead-approved; the 18 rows the lead struck are gone (the mask aural, kept struck after the lead was told that "aural fullness" then reads as aura; the chart red-flag phrases sudden onset headache, sudden-onset headache, facial numbness, aphasia, vision loss, visual loss, visual obscuration, jaw pain with chewing, jaw pain when chewing, jaw pain on chewing, periorbital swelling, periorbital edema, periorbital oedema, orbital swelling, eye pain, pain with eye movement and pain on eye movement); and the rows the lead approved at the sign-off are added (deny: not associated with, not accompanied by, neg for; hedge: +/-; rf_progressive: progressively worse, progressively worsening, worse each week; rf_asym: left-sided hearing loss, right-sided hearing loss, asymmetric hearing loss). Chart reading (clauses) applies to every line, typed chart text, spoken and demo lines alike (the lead's decision D9 of 2026-10-12; review round 2 had kept it to typed chart text): a statement, a pasted chart note or a spoken line is read clause by clause; a clause ends at . ! ? or ; followed by whitespace (a "?" opening a clause belongs to the words after it, so "? aura" is hedged; since review round 3 the "." of an abbreviation inside a sentence ends nothing: "No assoc. nausea."), at a line end that is not a wrapped line, after a section label, before a second "Label:" on a line of labels and before a break word, and never crosses a header. Every phrase and every negation, attribution and history cue matches only at a word start (wordStart); the clauses cue lists match as whole words, so "yes" never reads at the start of "yesterday"; and a phrase lying inside a mask word is no hit (mask: number, and since review round 2 the report headers ct showed, scope showed, lund-mackay, audiogram showed, hearing test showed, which name a test rather than its result, and hay fever). A mention is denied by a negation cue within the window inside its clause with no scopeEnd word between (a negation cue holding another at its end, as "didn't" holds "n't", is measured from that cue, so a contraction keeps its 0.3.2 reach), by a deny cue earlier in its clause, or on a line heading its list ("Patient denies:" over bullets or short lines), with no affirm cue between (a list denial, which a scopeEnd word or, since review round 3, a complement word ends, and which reaches a later list item only when that item is the finding alone: a mention it does not reach is set aside, recorded neither yes nor no; a window cue reaches a later item on the same terms), or by a post cue that closes the mention's item right after it (a ":", one word, or a list of findings it closes, between); an affirm cue between a negation cue and the mention keeps it affirmed, and one governing the mention keeps a post cue from denying it; a prefix cue glued to it drops the mention without recording a denial. A negation, deny, post or prefix cue lying inside a longer affirm or hedge cue is no cue ("no relief" holds "no ", "not sure" holds "not "); an affirm cue right after a finding (only a ":" or "-" between, or nothing before a sign such as "(+)") that closes the item answers it as a label and affirms it unless a denial in the label's own item governs it, and a deny cue so placed answers its label only and opens no list; a sign between two findings with only spaces around it is the prefix of the finding after it, and a plus sign before a word affirms it (review round 3). affirm (lead: endorses, reports, has, yes; lead-approved: endorsed, reported, admits, positive for, complains of, c/o, describes, presents with, (+), and the failed-treatment cues no improvement, no relief, no response, no benefit, without improvement, without relief, without benefit, failed, refractory to, despite); deny (lead: denies, no, lacks, doesn't have; lead-approved: denied, negative for, without, does not have, don't have, do not have, haven't had, hasn't had, (-), rather than, and since the sign-off not associated with, not accompanied by, neg for); post (lead-approved: negative, denied, absent, not present, : no, : none, (-), : denies, - no); prefix (lead-approved: non-, non); breaks (lead-approved: but, however, although, though, except, whereas, —, other than, besides, apart from); scopeEnd (lead-approved: with, so, now, until, is, are, was, were, to, from); complement (lead-approved, review round 3: for, in, about, after, since, on, none of). A yes/no item mentioned only affirmed records yes and only denied records no; one finding (the same phrase) both affirmed and denied records nothing and is asked instead, while different phrases of one item that disagree record yes (the affirmed mention wins: "It's not the weather … it's when I skip meals."), except for the rule-out items (strictConflict, lead-approved: x_purulent, x_objective, x_lowfreq, x_anosmia), where a "yes" lowers the index, so any affirmed and denied mention records nothing and is asked; context, scale and multi-answer entries take their first undenied mention in text order; in typed chart text a heard entry takes its duration only from its cue's own clause (a spoken line keeps release 0.4.6's band choice). A hedged clause (hedge: reportedly, possible, possibly, probable, questionable, suspected, unclear whether, unclear if, rule out, r/o, ?, maybe, unsure, uncertain, not sure, might, and since the sign-off +/-) and a clause holding unfilled template text (placeholder: ***, ___, [ ], []) record nothing; each is asked instead. Attribution and history windows stop at the clause; relatives named in chart wording are attribution cues (thirdParty: mother, father, mom, dad, sister, brother, daughter, son, parents, sibling, aunt, uncle, cousin, grandmother, grandfather, family history of, family hx of); in typed chart text the attribution cues "her " and "his " name the patient when a finding follows them and then do not gate (chartIgnoreThirdParty, lead-approved; a spoken line reads every cue, D19), while before any other word ("Her husband has tinnitus."), relatives and every other cue still gate.
